correctness.rationale: For n≥2 and 1≤k<n, uniform root splitting gives the exact f_k recursion with boundary values f_k(m)=0 (m<k), 1 (m=k), 2(m+1)/((k+1)(k+2)) (m>k). Expressing f_k(m) as its linear extension plus a finite defect yields zero defect mass, first moment k/3, second moment k(3k-1)/6. Conditioning on root rank and using symmetry then proves Cov((2I-(n-1))^2,X_{n,k})=4k(3k+1-2n)/(3n), including overlapping defect ranges. Exact enumeration of all insertion orders n=2..8 and rational finite-sum checks n=2..200 passed. Both global sum rules follow from the per-k formula; finite tests are supportive, not an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The identity gives the full finite-size response of all fringe-subtree size strata to an intuitive symmetric root-balance statistic. Its unique non-asymptotic sign switch at k=(2n-1)/3 explains why small-size and large-size components have opposing associations with root imbalance, while their weighted sum produces the known positive path-length covariance. The object is the classical BST subtree-size profile used in fringe analysis and tree-compression questions; the sharp complete classification is useful without a downstream theorem.
